The test image shows a soybean stem/hypocotyl with:
- Dark black necrosis/rot at the upper portion
- Tan/yellowish discoloration in the middle zone
- Dead, withered root tissue above
- Green healthy stem at the base

This is a stem rot pattern, likely damping-off or root rot. Top candidates: Phytophthora (dark stem canker), Pythium_damping_off, or Rhizoctonia. I'll use my 1 reference view on Phytophthora since the dark chocolate-brown to black stem lesion is most consistent.

The Phytophthora reference shows whole-plant wilting with brown leaves in wet soil — different presentation from the test image.

The test image shows a seedling with:
- Very dark black, collapsed hypocotyl tissue at the stem
- Sharp transition to tan/yellow below
- Dead/dried root tissue above
- Healthy green lower stem

This is a classic **post-emergence damping-off** pattern. The very dark water-soaked, collapsed hypocotyl is most characteristic of Pythium. Phytophthora tends more chocolate-brown and moves up the stem in older plants. Rhizoctonia shows reddish-brown with a wire-stem pattern. The dark black soft rot of the hypocotyl zone here best fits Pythium_damping_off.
